title: Pacing row menu 'Move to previous/next week': the toast reads 'Moved to undefined.' and the hint names a week the row does not go to
detail: Pacing › w/c 2 Nov › In class 'Binary Trees & Graph Traversal' › ⋯. The menu offers 'Move to previous week · w/c 26 Oct — HALF TERM'. Choosing it moves the row to w/c 19 Oct (wb 2026-11-02 → 2026-10-19, wk 9 → 8) and the toast says 'Moved to undefined.' with Undo (Undo works). Reproduced twice on dense at mac. The same mismatch shows for a personal row whose neighbour is a school-only week (w/c 14 Dec, no personal number) or a break. A move that fails ({ok:false}) also toasts 'Moved to undefined.' because the result object is truthy. Should: the hint names the week the row will land in, and the toast names it too.
rootCause: js/modules/pacing.js:1491 and 1507 read res.toWb, but moveEntryWeek returns {ok, prevWb, prevWk, wb, addedWeek} (js/modules/pacing.js:275), so weekAt(undefined) is null; `if (res)` is true for {ok:false}. The hints come from allWks[wkIdx±1] (js/modules/pacing.js:1478-1481), every week including breaks and the other register's weeks, while moveEntryWeek steps through weekListFor(e.source) (js/modules/pacing.js:252).
evidence: eval /tmp rowmove.js on dense mac: items ['Move to previous weekw/c 26 Oct — HALF TERM','Move to next weekw/c 9 Nov',…], after [2026-10-19, 8], toast ['Moved to undefined.\nUndo'], undone [2026-11-02, 9]; /Users/fj/Developer/KurenaiOS-519/audit-evidence/2026-12/shots/productivity/pacing-rowmove-toast-mac-dense.png
fix: Use res.wb and test res.ok; compute each hint from the same list moveEntryWeek uses (export weekListFor or a pure `neighbourWeek(e, ±1)`), and say 'Adds a new week' only when that list ends. Undo of a move that added a week should drop the week again when it is empty.

carbon.note: Confirmed P2: moveEntryWeek (js/modules/pacing.js:275) returns {ok, prevWb, prevWk, wb, addedWeek}, whereas menu handlers (:1491, :1507) test `if (res)` (truthy even on {ok:false}) and read `res.toWb` (undefined -> 'Moved to undefined.'), while menu hints (:1478-1481) read allWks[wkIdx±1] instead of weekListFor(e.source).

title: A hidden Pacing row still counts in the exam scope, 'next in pacing', and the month/term/year reports' plan totals
detail: Hide is a soft delete that every derived read must leave out (invariant 84). On dense, hiding personal row p46 ('Programming constructs…', w/c 12 Oct, ref 4.1.1.2, the only row with that ref): carriedInto(23 Nov) drops 25 → 24 and entriesFor leaves it out, but KOS.exams.pacingCovered('2026-11-26','compsci') stays at 52 leaves (the hidden row still puts 4.1.1.2 in an exam's 'covered by the plan' scope) and KOS.exams.nextInPacing('compsci:4.1.1.2') still answers 2026-10-12. A month/term/year report counts hidden personal rows in 'planned' and 'carried' while the week report does not.
rootCause: Readers use KOS.pacing.entries() (every row, hidden included, js/core/pacing.js:621) instead of entriesFor or a filter on hidden: js/core/exams.js:214 (pacingCovered), 602-604 (covered by a ticked row), 611 (nextInPacing); js/core/report.js:1275 (planRows for month/term/year; the week path at 1273 uses entriesFor and skips hidden); js/core/examsession.js:484 and js/modules/examprac.js:614 likewise.

fix: Give KOS.pacing a `visible()` read (entries().filter(e => !e.hidden)) and use it in every reader outside the page (exams.js, report.js, examsession.js, examprac.js, achcatalogue if wanted), or make entries() skip hidden and give the page an includeHidden option.

title: Calendar countdowns still count down to a showing you skipped ('Skip this showing' is ignored by nextOccurrence)
detail: Make a weekly Deadline due in 2 days (dense, harness), open it, Skip this showing for that date. occursOn(ev, that date) is false and the calendar grid drops it, but nextOccurrence still returns the skipped date, so Countdowns (the Calendar side card, Home, a subject's desk) still say '2 d' to 28 Nov instead of moving to 5 Dec. Opening that countdown row then shows the event as 'Skipped on Sat 28 Nov'. Reproduced twice (eval and again after cleanup).
rootCause: js/modules/calendar.js:444-463 nextOccurrence steps the rule arithmetically and never reads ev.skip or ev.ext.g.skip (occursOn does, js/modules/calendar.js:424-426); deadlines() (js/modules/calendar.js:506) and so countdowns() take its answer. Skip arrived in 1f251ebe (productivity#9).

fix: In nextOccurrence, after computing a candidate, advance while the candidate is skipped (loop with occursOn or step again, bounded); the reminders' own nextOccurrence is separate and unaffected.

carbon.note: Confirmed P2: js/modules/calendar.js:444-463 nextOccurrence advances recurrence arithmetically without consulting occursOn / ev.skip / ev.ext.g.skip, so deadlines() and countdowns() still target a skipped date.

title: Routines › Settings: switching the three reviews back from 'Per day' to 'Simple' silently overwrites every weekday time with Monday's, with no warning or Undo
detail: Sample account, mac. Routines › Settings › The three reviews › Per day; set Monday morning 06:30 and Tuesday 08:15 (slotTime: Mon 06:30, Tue 08:15, Wed 07:00, so U6 itself works). Press Simple: slots.morning.days is cleared and weekday becomes 06:30, so Tuesday's 08:15 is gone (slotTime Tue → 06:30). No confirm, no toast, no Undo; pressing Per day again rebuilds every day from the new simple times. Reproduced twice.
rootCause: js/modules/routines.js:695-704 (rvModeSeg onclick, the 'simple' branch): nextSlots[s] = {weekday: resolvedSlotDay(s, 1), weekend: resolvedSlotDay(s, 6), days: null}, written by V().setConfig at once.

fix: When the per-day times differ from what Simple can hold, ask first (KOS.ui.confirm: 'Use Monday's and Saturday's times for every day?') or keep `days` stored and stop reading it while Simple is on; either way give a toast with Undo that restores the previous slots.

title: Routine player drops a run step two levels down, so a routine that runs a routine that runs another can never be finished in the player ('1 of 2 · partial')
detail: Sample account, mac. Routines A (a1, run B), B (b1, run C), C (c1) — all accepted by KOS.routines.check (no loop). Open A's player: it lists 2 steps, 'a1' and '↻ AUDIT B · b1'; B's 'run C' step and C's c1 are missing. Press Done on every step: the player ends on 'AUDIT A · 1 of 2 · partial'; verdicts A 1/2, B 1/2, C 0/1. Ticking A's run step from the Today list instead works (A, B and C all kept), so only the player is wrong. Reproduced twice.
rootCause: js/modules/routineplayer.js:70-77 slots(): an inner routine's steps are flattened one level only and `if (x.checkMorning || x.run) return;` throws away the inner routine's own run steps instead of expanding them (or keeping them as one tickable step).
evidence: eval nest.js on sample mac: side ['a1','↻ AUDIT B','b1'], counter '1/2', after {A:{n:1,of:2}, B:{n:1,of:2}, C:{n:0,of:1}}, doneText 'AUDIT A · 1 of 2 · partial'; /Users/fj/Developer/KurenaiOS-519/audit-evidence/2026-12/shots/productivity/routine-player-nested-mac-sample.png
fix: Make slots() recursive (expand x.run with its own rid and group, guarded by a seen set like runsOf), or keep a nested run step as one step whose Done calls R().tick(x.rid, x.id, true) so tickRun handles the chain; or refuse a nested run in check() if one level is the design.

carbon.note: Confirmed P2: KOS.routines.check allows A -> run B -> run C (returns null), and ticking from Today cascades through tickRun, but js/modules/routineplayer.js:75 (`if (x.checkMorning || x.run) return;`) drops inner run steps after one level so C is never shown or ticked in the player.

detail: Copy account, iphone (402) and slide (375), #/calendar Agenda, week of 23 Nov. title: Finish and log on a sat paper logs an unmarked or part-marked paper as a real score (0/60, 2/60) with no warning — and simply viewing a part marks it 0
detail: F201 practice paper 3, dense account, mac: Start timed → Finish → confirm → on the marking screen (part 1(a) of 23 shown, nothing ticked) press 'Finish and log' in the bar. One attempt is logged as 0 of 60 (tracker uid jrk5arni, questions 1(a) got 0, the other 22 null); the Review shows 'Score 0 of 60', '▼ -2 on Practice paper 2', an estimated grade below Pass, and the tracker session pays (+8 XP, +1 gold). Paper 2 with only 1(a) and 1(b) ticked logged as 2 of 60, 'Marks lost 58 of 60', 'Below Pass, 22 to Pass'. 'Finish and log' sits in the bar from the first part on and asks nothing, although toAttempt has a 'not marked' path (marks null) and 'Mark later' exists. The attempt then feeds the exam's Practice cell, the trend, calibration and the grade/score goal (invariant 128 reads 'the best timed paper'). Reproduced on two sittings.
rootCause: js/modules/exampaperview.js:450/489 — drawing a part calls `tk(q.n, j)`, which creates an empty tick object; js/core/exampaper.js:274 `marked = !!(ticks[q.n] && ticks[q.n][j])` counts that empty object as marked (got 0), so the total becomes 0 instead of null; and logIt (exampaperview.js:550) sums only the marked parts and never warns that 22 of 23 are unmarked. KOS.attempts.setMarks (557) uses `Object.keys(m).length`, so the two records disagree.
evidence: /Users/fj/Developer/KurenaiOS-519/audit-evidence/2026-12/shots/exams-files-ink/after-log-ipadl-dense.png; eval KOS.tracker.all() for useq77yy → [k2q7ahpd 2/60], [jrk5arni 0/60, only 1(a) got 0]; sessions award {xp 8, gold 1, hp 2}
fix: In toAttempt treat a part as marked only when its tick object has a key (or a level was chosen); when parts remain unmarked, have Finish and log confirm 'n of 23 parts are not marked — log what you marked (scaled), or Mark later', and log marks null when none is marked.

carbon.note: Confirmed P1: js/modules/exampaperview.js:450,487 calls tk(q.n, j) when rendering a part, mutating M.ticks[q.n][j] = {}, and js/core/exampaper.js:274 treats any truthy ticks[q.n][j] object as marked (got: 0), so Finish and log records 0/60 (or partial marks out of 60) with no warning and pays a tracker session.

title: Ink Text tool: tapping the next table cell (or another spot) with the pen or mouse throws away what was typed in the open box — filling a table keeps only the last cell
detail: Topic 4.5.4.1, Handwritten tab, ipadl, mouse (a pen takes the same path). Add a table (UR-12), choose Text, tap cell A1 and type 'A1', tap B1 and type 'B1', tap C1 and type 'C1', then tap outside the page: the stored table is [['','','C1'],…] — A1 and B1 are gone. The same with free text boxes: type 'hello', tap lower down and type 'world' → only 'world' is stored. No message, no Undo for it. Reproduced three times (cells and free text). The only ways to keep a box are ⌘/Ctrl+Enter or tapping outside the page; Escape discards on purpose.
rootCause: js/core/inksurface.js:503-504 — openText begins with `closeText(false)` (discard), and the page's pointerdown (onDown, ~575-596) calls `e.preventDefault()` before opening the next box, so the open textarea never blurs and its blur handler (521, which closes with keep=true) never runs. The 1C table makes this the normal way to work (tap cell after cell); the free-text loss predates Phase 1 (same line at f479433b inkui.js:574).
evidence: /Users/fj/Developer/KurenaiOS-519/audit-evidence/2026-12/shots/exams-files-ink/ink-text-lost-ipadl-dense.png; /Users/fj/Developer/KurenaiOS-519/audit-evidence/2026-12/shots/exams-files-ink/ink-table-typing-ipadl-dense.png; eval listPages: table [['','','C1'],…], text 'world' only
fix: In openText call `closeText(true)` (keep) — Escape stays the discard path — so moving to another cell or spot saves the box first.

carbon.note: Confirmed P1: js/core/inksurface.js:504 calls closeText(false) at the start of openText, while onDown (:586) calls e.preventDefault() so the active textarea never blurs before the next cell/spot opens — discarding every typed table cell or text box except the last.

title: Once a past paper with the same bytes joins a written-on file, Files stops seeing its writing: the ✎ badge and 'Has my writing' drop it and 'Download with my writing' silently gives the original
detail: Files (dense, mac/ipadl): add worksheet.pdf, write two strokes on page 1 in the viewer (layer file:<fileId>:default, inked {page:2}); the card says '✎ 1 page' and Download gives 'worksheet (with my writing).pdf' with the strokes. Then import the same PDF into Exams › Practice › Paper files (any name). By design (invariant 150) the two show as one file, promoted to kind 'paper' with `alsoPaper` set. From then on KOS.files.writing(r) is 0: the card has no ✎, the 'Has my writing' filter hides it, and withWriting returns {ink:false, name:'worksheet.pdf'}, so Download/Share hand over the plain original with no message — invariant 151 says every Download or Share of a written-on file carries the writing. The writing is still in kurenai-os-ink and the viewer still shows it (it opens file:<fileId>:default), so it is hidden, not lost. Reproduced by eval and on the card.
rootCause: js/core/files.js:158 — `inkPrefix(r)` switches to 'paper:' + r.fileId + ':' as soon as `r.alsoPaper` is set, so the existing 'file:<fileId>:default' layer no longer matches; writing() (160-166) and latestLayer() (175-181) only add 'paper:<alsoPaper>:' and never look at the file: layer.
evidence: /Users/fj/Developer/KurenaiOS-519/audit-evidence/2026-12/shots/exams-files-ink/files-merged-open-ipadl-dense.png; /Users/fj/Developer/KurenaiOS-519/audit-evidence/2026-12/shots/exams-files-ink/download-with-writing-p1.png; eval record alsoPaper 'ppmwxrhurrbhsm1b', ink docs ['file:f90b3a96…:default {b1c2…:2}'], KOS.files.writing(r) 0, withWriting → {ink:false, name:'worksheet.pdf'}
fix: Have writing() and latestLayer() read both prefixes for a store-'files' record — 'file:<fileId>:' always, plus 'paper:<alsoPaper>:' when set — and keep inkPrefix for opening only.

carbon.note: Confirmed P1 (violates invariant 151): js/core/files.js:158 switches inkPrefix(r) from 'file:<fileId>:' to 'paper:<fileId>:' whenever r.alsoPaper is truthy, so writing() (:163) and latestLayer() (:177) stop checking 'file:<fileId>:' and return 0 / null even though the strokes remain in kurenai-os-ink.
carbon.evidence: Node repro: saved stroke to 'file:fid_test_1:default'; KOS.files.writing(r) returned 1 with alsoPaper:null and 0 with alsoPaper:'pap_99', and withWriting returned { name: 'worksheet.pdf', ink: false }.

title: Exam Plan ignores its own 'h a week': at '1 h a week' every week is planned at 2 h (3 h in the last week)
detail: An F201 real exam (12 Jan 2027) on the dense account, Plan section, budget select at '1 h a week' (the header reads '1 h a week for Real exam'). KOS.examSession.schedule(a) places 60 min in the first week, then 120 min in each of the next five weeks (topic 30 + paper 90) and 180 min in the week of 4 Jan (topic 30, paper 90, redo 30, cheat sheet 30). Week cards print '2 h 00' / '3 h 00' under a header promising 1 h. Send to the plan writes those rows into Pacing as they are. Reproduced twice (eval and the Plan screenshot). Expected: a paper that does not fit the week's hours is not placed (or the week shows that it is over, and the header's figure is the planned one).
rootCause: js/core/examsession.js:464 — `if (fits(d, pm) || !d.items.length) place(...)`: a paper is placed whenever its day is empty, even when `fits` says the week's minutes are spent; the redo, cheat-sheet and night-before items (458–460) are placed with no `fits` check at all.
evidence: /Users/fj/Developer/KurenaiOS-519/audit-evidence/2026-12/shots/exams-files-ink/exam-f201-plan-mac-dense.png; eval KOS.examSession.schedule(F201) → hours 1, weeks 60,120,120,120,120,120,180,20 min
fix: Drop the `|| !d.items.length` escape (or only allow it when the week has nothing yet and say 'over by n min' on the week card); run the fixed last-week items through `fits` too, or show the plan's real weekly total beside the budget.

carbon.note: Confirmed P2: at '1 h a week', js/core/examsession.js:464 places a 90-min paper whenever `!d.items.length` even though `fits(d, pm)` is false, and :458-460 places redo (30m), cheat sheet (30m), and night-before (20m) items with no `fits` check at all.

title: An authored F201 practice paper's side panel calls the papers 'Predicted paper 1/2/3', lists the paper you are on, and describes it as a shape-weighted draw
detail: Open #/exams/<F201>/paper/2 (or /1, /3). The 'Another paper' card offers 'Predicted paper 1 ›', 'Predicted paper 2 ›' (the paper already open) and 'Predicted paper 3 ›'. F201 has no Companion, so nothing is predicted (invariant 130: only a full Companion makes a predicted paper); the papers are the authored 'Practice paper 1 · Coastline Energy', '2 · Calderford City Council', '3 · Freshway'. 'Where the questions come from' says 'Original questions written by KurenaiOS for this paper's question shapes, weighted to its high-yield topics and to the shapes due by their pattern … The mark scheme names each question's shape' — none of which is true of an authored paper. 'This paper' says 'about 10 questions a sitting' for an 8-question paper. On paper 4 (a bank draw) the list correctly omits nothing but calls the authored papers just 'Practice paper 1/2/3'. Reproduced on papers 1 and 2, cold and warm.
rootCause: js/modules/exampaperview.js:110-117 — the side panel only knows 'practice' vs everything else, so kind 'authored' takes the predicted wording; the seed filter `n !== paper.seed` compares a number with the authored paper's string seed (js/core/exampaper.js:137 `seed: String(n)`), so the current paper is never excluded.

fix: Give 'authored' its own branch: 'Written whole by KurenaiOS in the board's format — not a board paper', title each link from KOS.examPaper.authoredList (e.g. 'Practice paper 2 · Calderford City Council'), compare seeds as numbers, and use bp.questions only for drawn papers.

carbon.note: Confirmed P2 (invariant 127, 130): js/modules/exampaperview.js:110-118 branches only on `paper.kind === 'practice'`, sending `kind === 'authored'` (OCR F201 papers 1–3) down the Companion 'Predicted paper' copy path, while `n !== paper.seed` compares number `n` against string `paper.seed` ('2'), failing to exclude the currently open paper.

title: Right after Finish and log, Review says the attempt 'has no recorded journal: it was logged, not sat in the app' — the journal link is still being written

title: Marking a sat paper on iPad: the scheme's tick chips are 26 px tall — their coarse-pointer 44 px rule is overridden by the base rule below it
detail: ipadl (pointer: coarse), the marking screen after Finish: each scheme line's '○ ✓' chip (exams.mchip, also the level's 'a mark inside it' chips) measures 44×26. These are the controls you press most while marking on the iPad. Reproduced at ipadl and ipad.

carbon.note: Confirmed P2 (invariant 69): css/views/exams.css:820 places `@media (pointer: coarse) { .k-ex-mchip { min-block-size: var(--hit-coarse); ... } }` above the equal-specificity base rule `.k-ex-mchip { min-block-size: var(--sp-26); ... }` at :823, overriding the 44 px coarse-pointer floor down to 26 px.

title: '+ Log error' on the Ink tab and the exam Review does nothing on its first press after a load: the Error Log capture asks a lazy-loader method that does not exist
detail: Cold-load a topic page (ipadl), open Handwritten and press '+ Log error' within the first seconds: no sheet opens (KOS.errorLogUI false before, no .k-dialog-overlay 3 s later). The same on a cold exam Review's Marks lost card '+ Log error' (mac). A second press later works, only because the background warm-up has loaded page-errorlog by then; with Save-Data on (lazy.js:291 skips warming) it would never open until the Error Log page is visited. The post-mortem's costly-card pill works (it logs without the sheet). Also: the Review's capture saves topicRef null and topicTitle = the paper's title, so the Error Log hub lists 'Practice paper 2 · Real exam' as an error-prone TOPIC, and its deep link opens the exam's latest review, not this attempt. Reproduced twice on each surface.
rootCause: js/core/errorlog.js:166 — `if (KOS.lazy && KOS.lazy.ensure) KOS.lazy.ensure(["page-errorlog"], openNow)`: KOS.lazy has no `ensure` (js/core/lazy.js:519 exports need/needs/…), so when the bundle is not in yet openCapture silently returns. js/modules/examreview.js:132-143 passes no topicRef and a deepLink without `sub: 'a:' + e.uid`.
evidence: /Users/fj/Developer/KurenaiOS-519/audit-evidence/2026-12/shots/exams-files-ink/review-logerror-cold-mac-dense.png; /Users/fj/Developer/KurenaiOS-519/audit-evidence/2026-12/shots/exams-files-ink/review-logerror-second-mac-dense.png; eval cold ink tab: {before:false, after:true, dialog:false}; error entry err_gh3rk42nps topicRef null
fix: Use `KOS.lazy.need('page-errorlog').then(openNow)`; on the Review pass the costliest lost topic as topicRef (lossCols already has it) and `sub: 'a:' + e.uid` in the deep link.

carbon.note: Confirmed P2: two distinct bugs verified — (1) js/core/errorlog.js:166 calls non-existent KOS.lazy.ensure (shared with ST-47), dropping cold '+ Log error' taps on Handwritten and Exam Review; (2) js/modules/examreview.js:116-124 passes no topicRef and sets topicTitle to the paper title with deepLink missing `sub: 'a:' + e.uid`.

title: 'Download with my writing' (and Download the original) on the Mac opens the share sheet instead of downloading
detail: Files page on mac (Chrome, which supports Web Share with files): ⋯ › 'Download with my writing' on a written-on PDF calls navigator.share with 'worksheet (with my writing).pdf' (17,344 bytes; its writing is correctly flattened onto page 1) instead of saving it. The same path serves 'Download the original', a topic's Files tab and the viewer's Save a copy. On macOS the share sheet has no plain 'save to Downloads', so the menu item named Download does not download; on the iPad the sheet's Save to Files is a fair stand-in. Reproduced twice with navigator.share stubbed to capture the call; with share available no anchor download ever fires.
rootCause: js/core/inkexport.js:115-123 — deliver() prefers navigator.share whenever navigator.canShare({files}) is true, for every caller; js/modules/files.js:159-163 'download' calls deliver, not download().
evidence: /Users/fj/Developer/KurenaiOS-519/audit-evidence/2026-12/shots/exams-files-ink/download-with-writing-p1.png; eval navigator.canShare(files) true on mac; captured share call ['worksheet (with my writing).pdf 17344']
fix: Give deliver a mode: Download items call KOS.inkExport.download (anchor) on a fine pointer / non-touch device and keep the share sheet for Share and for touch iPad/iPhone.

carbon.note: Confirmed P2: js/modules/files.js:159-163 routes explicit 'Download' menu actions through `KOS.inkExport.deliver` (js/core/inkexport.js:115-123), which invokes `navigator.share({ files })` whenever `navigator.canShare` returns true — opening the macOS Share sheet instead of downloading on desktop Chrome/Safari.

title: Files added before the one-file-per-hash change (v3) never got a hash: adding the same file again stores a second copy and Files shows it twice — 12 of the copy's 25 files
detail: Copy account: 12 of 25 records in kurenai-os-files have hash null (added July-October 2026; 11 still hold their bytes, among them 10 CS 4.5.1.1 papers/schemes and an IT handout). Re-adding one of them (its own blob as a new File) through KOS.attach.add, (1) to another topic → {linked:false}, record 31 stored with a real hash, the old one still null; (2) to the SAME topic → {linked:false}, record 32 stored. Files then lists both copies (two size groups duplicated) — invariant 150 says one file per hash with many links. The same holds for the paper twin rule (files.js:76 twin = r.hash && hashes[r.hash]): a Paper-library PDF with the same bytes never joins such a file. Test records removed afterwards (count back to 25).
rootCause: js/modules/attachments.js:73-86 — the v3 upgrade back-fills fileId, updatedAt and linkKeys for old rows but never computes hash; add() (attachments.js:169-192) looks up the hash index, which an old row (hash null) can never match. Only Paper-library records get a hash back-fill (js/core/exampapers.js:216-220).
evidence: /Users/fj/Developer/KurenaiOS-519/audit-evidence/2026-12/shots/copy/files-mac-copy-dupe-readd.png; eval nullHash 12/25, add → {id:31, linked:false}, add same topic → {id:32, linked:false}; js/modules/attachments.js:73
fix: A one-time idle back-fill: for records with a blob and no hash, hashOf(blob) → updateFile(rec.fileId, r.hash = h), then merge any two records that now share a hash through the existing link path (KOS.repairs if it merges); mirror exampapers.js:216.

carbon.note: Confirmed P2 (invariant 150): js/modules/attachments.js:73-86 v3 IndexedDB upgrade back-filled `fileId`, `updatedAt`, and `linkKeys` without computing `hash`, so pre-v3 files carry `hash: null` and fail deduplication and past-paper twin pairing when re-added.

title: Copy as TeX keeps a reply with a sentence before its code fence: 'Sure! ```latex …```' renders (as italic prose) and goes on the page
detail: Lasso a stroke → Copy as TeX… → paste the reply 'Sure! ```latex\n\frac{1}{2} + x^2\n```' (what a chat model often sends despite the prompt). The preview renders 'Sure!‘‘‘latex ½ + x²‘‘‘' and 'Keep it on the page' is enabled, so the junk is kept as a tex item. A reply of just the fenced block is cleaned correctly, and one with '$$' inside prose is refused with a KaTeX error. The 'kept only once KaTeX renders it' guard does not catch prose, because KaTeX renders words as maths italics.
rootCause: js/core/ink.js:282-291 cleanTex strips a fence only when it spans the whole reply (`/^```…```$/`) and the $ pairs only at both ends; js/modules/inktex.js:30-35 texCheck accepts anything KaTeX renders.
evidence: /Users/fj/Developer/KurenaiOS-519/audit-evidence/2026-12/shots/exams-files-ink/ink-tex-good-ipadl-dense.png; /Users/fj/Developer/KurenaiOS-519/audit-evidence/2026-12/shots/exams-files-ink/ink-tex-bad-ipadl-dense.png
fix: In cleanTex take the first fenced block found anywhere in the reply (and the first $$…$$ / \[…\] span) before checking; optionally refuse a result containing a run of plain words.

carbon.note: Confirmed P3: `KOS.ink.geo.cleanTex` (js/core/ink.js:282-291) anchors fence stripping to `/^```...```$/`, leaving leading chat prose intact, and KaTeX renders plain words + backticks as maths italics/quotes without throwing.
carbon.evidence: Node repro: KOS.ink.geo.cleanTex('Sure! ```latex\n\\frac{1}{2} + x^2\n```') returned the unstripped string verbatim.

title: Error Log: the inline pill's 'Undo' beside a re-shown question permanently deletes an older entry, notes and all, with no confirm or Undo
detail: Log a mistake from an exam self-mark (or a quiz miss), then later write 'What went wrong' / 'Rule for next time' and tags on it in the hub. Come back to the same question and reveal the mark scheme: the pill finds the existing open entry by its dedupeKey and draws '✓ Logged · Tag reason' + 'Undo'. One tap on Undo deletes the whole entry, including the user's written notes and tags. No confirm, no toast, no way back; the hub's own Delete (inside Edit) at least offers an Undo toast. Measured on Sample, CS 4.2.1.2 exam Q1: entry err_5jpnot0s73 with wrongNote/ruleNote/mistakeTypes set; after Undo it is gone from state.errorLog.items, #toast is empty and the pill is back to '+ Log mistake'. Reproduced twice.
rootCause: js/core/errorlog.js:176 adopts ANY open entry with the same dedupeKey as the pill's own 'entry', and the Undo button at js/core/errorlog.js:195-196 calls remove(entry.id) unconditionally, so 'Undo' acts on an entry this pill never created
evidence: /Users/fj/Developer/KurenaiOS-519/audit-evidence/2026-12/shots/study-core/topic-cs42112-exam-reveal-mac-sample.png; eval: KOS.errorLog.update(id,{wrongNote,ruleNote,mistakeTypes}) → reopen exam tab → Reveal → click [data-ui~=quiz.log-undo] → entry DELETED, toast ''
fix: Offer Undo only for an entry this pill created in this render (quickLog's existed=false); for an adopted entry show only '✓ Logged · Tag reason' (opening the editor, whose Delete has the Undo toast). If a remove stays, route it through the same toast-with-restore as the dialog's Delete.

carbon.note: Confirmed P1: js/core/errorlog.js:176 adopts any open entry matching dedupeKey, and the inline pill's Undo button (:195-196) calls remove(entry.id) unconditionally with no confirmation and no Undo toast, permanently deleting older user-written wrongNote/ruleNote/mistakeTypes.

title: A pull that re-keys a colliding record while its editor is open makes Save overwrite the OTHER device's record (goals, assignments and every counter-id record edited by object)
detail: Two devices each add a goal between syncs, both get goals.nextId = 10 (goals still mint per-device counter ids). On this device the goal editor is open on its goal 10 ('LOCAL goal: 10 h of CS', title edited to '…12 h… (edited)'). A pull lands: the merge correctly re-keys the local goal to 11 and keeps the other device's goal as 10 ('REMOTE goal: read 3 books', target 3). The editor stays open; Save writes the edited fields with G.update(existing.id = 10, …): final {id:11, 'LOCAL goal: 10 h of CS', target 10 — edit lost}, {id:10, 'LOCAL goal: 12 h of CS (edited)', target 10 — the other device's goal overwritten}. The next push sends the overwrite to the other device: its goal is gone everywhere, and the edit went to the wrong record. Same with an assignment holding a numeric id (k1.js: the other device's 'REMOTE lab report' maths/inProgress/40%/notes replaced by the local essay's fields). Reproduced at ipad (k1.js assignments, k2.js goals). New assignments, reminders and events take random ids since 1A, but goals, pacing rows, tracker entries, resources, wishlist items, todo items and oop classes still mint counter ids (cloudmerge.js RECORDS), so a collision needs only two devices adding a record before they sync.
rootCause: js/core/store.js:807-822 assignList (applyDoc, used by replaceState since 1A bk:data-integrity#5) keeps object identity BY ID: after cloudmerge re-keys the local record (cloudmerge.js:66-110 RECORDS, invariant 33a), the object that held the local record is matched to the merged record that now owns its old id — the OTHER device's — and filled with its fields; the re-keyed local record becomes a new object. Editors hold the record object and save by its id: js/modules/goals.js:1048/1076 G.update(existing.id, fields), js/modules/assignments.js:356/443 A().update(existing.id, patch). title: A first link drops this device's Pacing row customisations (U4 hidden, order, day): pacingTouched does not see them, so the account's plan replaces it
detail: U4 added per-row `hidden`, `order` and `day` to Pacing rows. The first-link (no-base) merge replaces this device's whole `pacing` with the account's whenever `pacingTouched` says the device never touched its plan (stripSeeds, js/core/cloudsync.js:474), and `KOS.cloudsync.userData` uses the same test to decide whether the device holds data at all. Measured in the test harness (userdata_u4.js, run twice): on a pristine boot (252 seeded rows) setting entries[0].hidden = true, or order on two rows, or day = 4, leaves userData() === null; flipping `done` returns 'pacing'. So a device whose plan edits are only hides, reorders or weekday moves (and any device at all, when its other data is elsewhere) has those edits overwritten by the account's plan on its first sign-in: hidden rows come back, the order and weekdays reset. The same test also ignores the Daily Review's configuration (`dayReview.config`, incl. U6's per-day slot times): a device whose only change is its review times reads as pristine (userData null) and adopts the account's.

title: A question schedule whose item is gone (504 removed by the study clean-up, or a fork deletion) is still due for ever: it is counted in 'questions back today' and takes one of the subject's daily cap slots
detail: KOS.questions.dueToday() reads every q:/e: key in state.srs (scheduled(), js/core/questions.js:163-170) without asking whether the item still exists; the Due run then passes over a key whose item is gone (js/modules/due.js:341-344). Nothing ever moves or drops that schedule, so it stays overdue for ever. Measured in the test harness (orphan_one.js, twice): 10 real compsci 4.2.1.1 questions due today plus the schedule of q:compsci:4.2.1.1:4 ('Which statement about a static data structure is correct?', removed by the clean-up 3ca78aa5) → dueToday() {total:10, waiting:1, by.compsci:{due:11, cap:10, left:10}}, the orphan holds a cap slot, only 9 runnable, and one real question is pushed to 'waiting'. The Review page's count (due.js:114, 142, 159) says 10 questions while the run serves 9. With N orphans in a subject, N of its 10 daily slots are lost every day; at 10 the subject's questions never come back. Flashcards are not affected (dueCards walks allCards, js/core/srs.js:468), but Home's 'learnt' fact counts every srs key with reps > 0, orphans included (js/modules/home.js:1050). Invariant 87/111c keys themselves hold: the kept items carry their old place (`oi` / third element), spot-checked on 4.2.1.1 (quiz ids 0,1,2,3,5..9; exam 0..3). The user's own data copy was not available, so how many orphans the real account holds is not measured; questions joined the schedule on 16 Nov, so any removed item answered since then is one.
rootCause: js/core/questions.js:163-170 — scheduled() lists keys from state.srs, not from the effective material; dueToday() (174-201) counts and caps them before the page resolves them with itemOf().

title: Taking a document in place (cloud land, another tab's save, Restore) merges two rows that share an id into one object: the first row's data is overwritten and saved
detail: store.js applyDoc → assignDeep → assignList keeps each row's identity by indexing the CURRENT array by typeof+id and, for every incoming row, re-using the matching current object. When an array holds two rows with the same id, both incoming rows map to the SAME current object: it is assigned the first row, then overwritten with the second, and pushed twice. Measured in the test harness, twice each: (1) Daily Review picks — dayReview.days[d].morning.three = [{kind:'reminder',id:3},{kind:'assignment',id:3},{kind:'event',id:7}] through KOS.store.replaceState(copy of the same state) → memory AND localStorage hold [{assignment 3},{assignment 3},{event 7}]: the reminder pick is gone (review_three_apply.js). Old reminders and assignments both counted from 1 (pre-1A), so a review naming 'reminder 12' and 'assignment 12' is ordinary data. (2) Two ledger entries with id 5 (a focus session on 1 Sep, a quiz on 2 Sep) → after replaceState localStorage holds two copies of the quiz; the focus session, its minutes and its day are lost (dupid_apply.js: storedBefore [[5,1000,'focus'],[5,2000,'quiz']] → storedAfter [[5,2000,'quiz'],[5,2000,'quiz']]). js/core/sessions.js:32-34 says older ledgers may already hold such duplicate ids. The same path runs on EVERY cloud document landing (33d, since 1A 373d8104), every adopt of another tab's write (33c takeIn, since RC5 af71fd27) and every Restore or checkpoint restore (importFull → replaceState) — so the safety net itself corrupts what it restores. KOS.cloudmerge.merge on the same document does not (it re-keys the duplicate, 5 → 6). The user's own data copy was not available, so whether their ledger holds duplicate-id sessions is unmeasured; if it does, this is silent ledger loss on every pull (P0 grade). The seeded test account holds none (dupscan.js).
rootCause: js/core/store.js:807-822 — assignList builds byId from dst and returns the same matched object for every src row with that key (no 'used' marker, no check that ids are unique within the array); arrays of refs like the review's {kind,id} picks share ids across kinds by design.
evidence: /Users/fj/Developer/KurenaiOS-519/audit-evidence/2026-12/shots/data-integrity/review_three_apply.js → {"memory":[{"kind":"assignment","id":3},{"kind":"assignment","id":3},{"kind":"event","id":7}],"stored":[same]}; dupid_apply.js + inline probe → storedAfter [[5,2000,"quiz"],[5,2000,"quiz"]], mergeSame [[6,1000,"focus"],[5,2000,"quiz"]]
fix: In assignList re-use a dst object at most once (delete it from byId when taken) and fall back to plain replacement for an array whose src ids are not unique (or whose rows carry `kind`: key such rows by kind+id). Add a smoke196 case: duplicate ids and mixed-kind {kind,id} picks survive replaceState, takeIn and importFull unchanged.

title: A deleted exam attempt comes back for a sync cycle: kos_attempts pulls BEFORE it pushes its tombstone, and the two-minute overlap re-delivers the row
detail: Measured with KOS.attempts and an injected fake cloud (KOS.attempts._setCloudApi, server-stamped updated_at; attempts_resurrect.js, run twice): record and end an attempt, sync twice (pushed 1, then the echo skipped), wait, delete it (local list 0, tombstone queued in attempts.del), sync → {pushed:1, pulled:1}: the pull ran first with the overlap (KOS.sideSync.since), found the row it no longer holds and put it back (local list 1); the tombstone then reached the server. Only the NEXT cycle pulls the tombstone and deletes it (local 0). After a delete the next run is soonSync's 20 s, then nothing until the 30-minute timer or another change, so the attempt sits in the list, the paper's stats and readiness for up to half an hour. Because the cursor is the newest row's own stamp, this hits any deletion of the most recently synced attempt. Money and Mind push first and skip their echo by stamp (js/core/money.js syncCloud, js/core/mindjournal.js:205-246), so they do not. A second, narrower gap: the push ends with kvSet('attempts.del', []) (attempts.js:340), wiping a tombstone that remove() added while the upload was in flight, so that deletion never reaches the server or the other devices.
rootCause: js/core/attempts.js:292-347 — syncCloud pulls first and treats a pulled row this device does not hold (`mine` undefined after a local delete) as new, without consulting the pending tombstones in attempts.del; and clears the whole tombstone list after the push instead of only the uids it sent.

fix: Push before pull (invariant 33's order, as money/mind do), or skip a pulled uid that is in attempts.del; after the push remove only the tombstones whose uids were sent.

title: The service worker mixes versions after a deploy: stale-while-revalidate writes the new deploy's scripts into the old version's cache, so the old index.html runs new scripts until the update is accepted
detail: sw.js says 'a page is always one version' and serves navigations from the index.html cached with the worker's own VERSION (sw.js:255-273, invariant 37). But every same-origin script and stylesheet is stale-while-revalidate into that SAME cache (sw.js:186-199, 280): the first load after a deploy serves the old copy and, in the background, puts the NEW deploy's file into kos-static-<OLD VERSION>. The new worker meanwhile waits for the user's 'Reload now' (invariant 38). If the user says Later, or simply reloads/relaunches the PWA, the next load pairs the old index.html (old template/bundle lists, old script order) with whichever new scripts were refreshed — each file switching only when it is next requested, so lazy bundles stay old until opened. A release that adds a file, moves a function between files or changes a boot part/page part split (1F did all three) can then throw at boot or miss a page part. Reproduced twice with the project's own worker harness: tools/smoke121.test.js step C evaluates sw.js, deploys B, fetches js/core/store.js twice from worker A and logs 'note C: SWR put deploy B's js/core/store.js into kos-static-kos-smoke-a — A's shell now loads B's script (mixed version until the update is accepted)'; the suite records it as a note, never a failure, since 8 Nov (969371e4). It is in no November finding and not in the QoL plan (architecture-perf#3 there is only about re-downloading). A live repro on a non-dev host was attempted (a copy served as kos.test) but the headless worker's precache did not finish in that setup, so the evidence is the worker harness and the code.
rootCause: sw.js:280 staleWhileRevalidate(e, STATIC_CACHE) for every same-origin GET, with STATIC_CACHE = 'kos-static-' + VERSION (sw.js:44-45) shared with the shell served at sw.js:261-264; cache.put of the network response at sw.js:190

fix: Serve precached same-origin statics CACHE-FIRST from the worker's own version cache with no background refresh (the precache is already derived from index.html, and a deploy bumps VERSION, invariant 38), keeping SWR only for the CDN runtime cache; anything not precached may go network-then-cache. Turn smoke121's note C into an assertion that A's cache never receives B's bytes.

title: A verified checkpoint of the real account is one 56.7 MB string: 8-13 s at 4x CPU and ~485 MB of extra heap, and the first cloud link, every import, reset and repair waits on it
detail: Copy account (the user's 26 Nov backup): KOS.backup.checkpoint('…') at 4x CPU took 12.7 s at mac and 8.0 s at iphone, ok:true, bytes 56.7 MB, and the page's used JS heap rose by 487 MB and 482 MB while it ran (performance.memory before/after, two runs). One checkpoint holds the snapshot object, its JSON text, the text read back from IndexedDB, its parse and a second live snapshot at once (backup.js:168-196), which is where the heap goes. Five are kept: about 280 MB of IndexedDB on this account. The streamed backup FILE of the same data (KOS.backupFile.write, DI-09) builds in about 1 s with nothing missing. CLAUDE.md names the one-string checkpoint as a known limit for a very large file set; this account is already there because of ink alone, and it grows with every page written. On an iPhone or iPad tab a ~0.5 GB spike risks the WebContent process being killed in the middle of 'Before linking this device to the cloud' (cloudsync.js:879-881), which the first link requires (invariant 34), or before an import/reset (dataview.js:106, 345).
rootCause: js/core/backup.js:168-196 attempt() — JSON.stringify of the whole snapshotFull (backup.js:136-141, store.js:1335) into one string, stored as one record, read back whole and parsed whole, then snapshotFull again for the live check; nothing is split per part or streamed as KOS.backupFile already does.

fix: Store a checkpoint as one record per part (and per file / per ink doc), each with its own SHA-256, and verify part by part — reuse KOS.backupFile's per-line layout — so no step holds the whole account as one string; keep fewer checkpoints when they are large.

title: KOS.errorLog.openCapture asks for KOS.lazy.ensure, which lazy.js never defined, and the existence guard hides it: every Error Log capture before page-errorlog is in does nothing
detail: Root cause of ST-47 and EX-57, checked across the codebase. title: Global search's Exams & Papers domain throws 'all.filter is not a function' on every query, making all assessments unsearchable
detail: Add any assessment in Exams & Papers (or use the seeded/sample exams) and search its title, subject, or paper in global search (`KOS.search.run`). Once the `search-more` bundle loads, `examsDomain` reads `KOS.store.state.exams.assessments` — which is a keyed object map `{ [id]: assessment }` (invariant 120), never an Array — and calls `all.filter(...)`. That throws `TypeError: all.filter is not a function` on every search keystroke; `KOS.search.run`'s `safe()` wrapper (`js/core/search.js:331`) catches and silences the exception, so global search returns 0 exam matches on every account and viewport.
rootCause: js/core/searchmore.js:104-106 — `var all = (ex && ex.assessments) || []; var out = all.filter(...)` treats the `state.exams.assessments` object map as an array instead of calling `KOS.exams.all()` or `Object.values(...)`; `js/core/search.js:331` swallows the thrown TypeError.
evidence: Node boot + KOS.lazy.all() + KOS.exams.add({title:'UniqueQuantumExam2027',...}): typeof state.exams.assessments === 'object' (Array.isArray false); KOS.search.run('UniqueQuantumExam2027', cb) returned [] on done=true; calling KOS.search.more.sync[2] directly threw 'TypeError: all.filter is not a function'.
fix: In `js/core/searchmore.js:105`, read `var all = KOS.exams && KOS.exams.all ? KOS.exams.all() : Object.values((ex && ex.assessments) || {});` and add a smoke assertion that `KOS.search.run` finds an added assessment by title.

title: cloudmerge merges state.srs and state.code.cards field by field instead of atomically by latest review, discarding newer reviews and creating chimera FSRS/leech records
detail: When two devices review the same curriculum/custom flashcard, scheduled `q:`/`e:` question (`state.srs[key]`), or Code card (`state.code.cards[id]`) before syncing — or one device un-leeches a card (`leech: null, leechBase: 8`) while the other reviewed it — `KOS.cloudmerge.merge` merges the FSRS record key-by-key instead of keeping the more recent review whole. On a three-way merge where Local rated Good on 2026-09-20 (`s: 25, due: '2026-10-15'`) and Remote rated Again on 2026-09-24 (`s: 1.5, due: '2026-09-25', lapses: 8, leech: true`), Local wins same-key conflicts (`preferRemote: false`), discarding Remote's newer review and keeping `s: 25, due: '2026-10-15'`, while grafting Remote's newly added `leech: true` (or `leechBase`) onto the same record — leaving a corrupted chimera schedule.
rootCause: js/core/cloudmerge.js:141,496-521 — `FACET_PATH = /^(japanese\.facets|mind\.cards)\.[^.]+$/` protects only Japanese facets and Mind cards; `srs.<key>` (whose keys also contain dots, e.g. `compsci:4.5.2.1:0`) and `code.cards.<id>` fall through to plain-object per-field `mergeValue`.
evidence: Node repro via KOS.cloudmerge.merge(base, local, remote): `merged.doc.srs['compsci:4.2.1.1:0']` produced `{ reps: 8, lapses: 8, s: 25, d: 6.5, ivl: 25, due: '2026-10-15', last: '2026-09-20', leech: true }` (Remote's newer Sep 24 review lost while its `leech: true` was grafted onto Local's Sep 20 schedule); `code.cards['u1-swap']` similarly mixed Local's `s: 6, due: '2026-09-26'` with Remote's `lapses: 1`.
fix: Widen `FACET_PATH` in `js/core/cloudmerge.js:141` to `/^(japanese\.facets\.[^.]+|mind\.cards\.[^.]+|code\.cards\.[^.]+|srs\..+)$/` (every `srs[key]` record holds primitive fields only) and break `last` ties safely so `leech`/`leechBase` and FSRS stability/due always travel together; add a regression case in `smoke135`/`smoke146`.
phase1: Phase 1 `leechBase` (`js/core/srs.js:268`) widened the chimera surface; base `srs`/`code.cards` omission predates Phase 1

title: redraw.js READS omits state keys read by five views (#/files misses folders, #/mind/daily misses exams, #/calendar misses sessions, #/code and #/japanese miss errorLog), and smoke139 N fails to cover them
detail: Horizontal Sweep 1 against invariant 164 found five undeclared top-level state dependencies in `js/core/redraw.js`: (1) `READS.files` (:96) and `STUDY` (:54, for a topic's Files tab) omit `'folders'` (1C UR-14 `state.folders`, read by `js/modules/files.js:263` and `js/core/files.js:145`), so creating, renaming, or deleting a folder in another tab or via cloud sync leaves `KOS.changes.relevant('files', null, ['folders']) === false` (no chip, no redraw; and `files.js:217` only clears a deleted `p.folder` on full view remount, not inside `paintFolders()`); (2) `READS.mind` (:73) omits `'exams'`, though `#/mind/daily` (`js/modules/mind.js:689,742-753` -> `KOS.mind.daily()`) reads `state.exams` to switch into `'Exam Season: reviews only'`; (3) `READS.calendar` (:77) omits `'sessions'`, though `js/modules/calendar.js:595` (`KOS.exams.startState` -> `startBy` -> `weeklyHours`) reads `state.sessions` to compute derived exam start-by dates; (4) `READS.code` (:71) and `READS.japanese` (:72) omit `'errorLog'`, though `js/modules/code.js:792` and `js/modules/jarun.js:580` mount `KOS.errorLog.inlinePill` (reading `state.errorLog`). `smoke139 N` missed all five because `seedAccount` seeds 0 files/folders and no active exam `startBy`, `SURF.reads` only traps keys already present on `Object.keys(state)`, and `tools/lib/view-surfaces.js` omits `['mind', { page: 'daily' }]` and post-answer study states.
rootCause: js/core/redraw.js:54,71-73,77,96 missing `'folders'`, `'exams'`, `'sessions'`, and `'errorLog'`; js/modules/files.js:261 `paintFolders()` not resetting deleted `p.folder`; tools/lib/view-surfaces.js:20,28,42 lacking seeded file/folder/exam coverage and `mind:daily`.
evidence: Node repro: (1) on `#/files` with a file attached, mutating `state.folders` gave `KOS.changes.diff === ['folders']`, `KOS.changes.relevant('files', null, ['folders']) === false`, `pending === null`; (2) running `SURF.reads` with optional state keys, 1 file, and 1 exam seeded immediately flagged `MISS: calendar -> ['sessions']`, `MISS: files -> ['folders']`, `MISS: mind {"page":"daily"} -> ['exams']`.

title: Phase 1 Universal Error Log (`state.errorLog`) is missing from global search, Assistant domain tools, document tallies, cloudmerge `SET_FIELDS`, and flashcard-push Undo
detail: Omission hunt + Sweep 1.4 across Phase 1's Universal Error Log (`f479433b..fa4264d0`) found five cross-cutting contract omissions: (1) Global search (`js/core/search.js`, `js/core/searchmore.js`, invariant 71) adds only the static `'Error Log'` page row in `PAGES` (`7734300b`) and never searches `state.errorLog.items` (`title`, `wrongNote`, `ruleNote`, `topicTitle`); (2) Assistant tools (`js/core/aitools.js:2796`, invariant 71a: 'Assistant tools cover every domain') only adds `'errorlog'` to `navigate`'s enum, with zero read/log/resolve tools for `KOS.errorLog`; (3) `KOS.store.tally()` (`js/core/store.js:1146`) omits `errorLog.items` from Restore and first-link before/after counts; (4) `SET_FIELDS` (`js/core/cloudmerge.js:124`) omits `mistakeTypes`, so two devices tagging different mistake types on the same entry do not union them as a set; (5) `toFlashcard` (`js/modules/errorlog.js:437-442,753-759`) creates a custom card and sets `cardId` with a plain toast lacking Undo, contrary to `js/modules/errorlog.js:4` ('every write passes through KOS.errorLog with Undo').
